r: **Revolution of the Earth + inclination (tilt) of its axis**
**Revolution on a tilted axis** – not rotation, the elliptical orbit, oceans, mountains or altitude
**23½° (23.5°) from the perpendicular** = **66½° to the orbital plane**
Axis keeps pointing the same way (towards the **Pole Star**) all year because of **angular momentum** → hemispheres tilt alternately towards (summer) and away (winter) → **opposite seasons**
**Axial inclination + parallelism + revolution + spherical shape** → changing **angle of insolation** and **day length**
Seasons, unequal days, the tropics and polar circles
Day and night (the **circle of illumination** divides them) and the **Coriolis** deflection, to the **right in the NH**
No seasons, equal day and night all year, Sun always over the Equator; the North Pole would not lie always in darkness

2.x: Earth is **nearest the Sun in northern winter**, so distance does not cause seasons.

Long term: **precession** (axial wobble) – **Vega** was pole star ~14,000 years ago and will be again in ~12,000 years; **Milankovitch cycles** drive long-term climate change. Melting ice moving mass away from the axis **slows rotation**.
Seasons come from **revolution on an inclined axis** – not from rotation or the Sun's distance.
